title: inspect-v2 recorded answer
description: The one recorded answer of an inspect-v2 run, handed to `record-answer --answer FILE` (references/inspect-v2-contract.md section 7). It is two documents in one file: the executor's (the shared fields every front core's answer carries, `questions` and `lines`, plus `row`, `owner_word`, `lanes`, `adjudications`, `hunted_and_held` and `bottom_line`) and, under `results`, the readers' results, one per lens call, each carrying the reader's call id, row, effective model and findings exactly as the READERS: line and the reply gave them. Closed at every level: an unknown key is refused, never ignored, so a clear (`disposition`, `waived`) can never ride in. What a schema cannot say is checked by `record-answer` in code (the shared E14-11 refusals through station_core/answer.py, then this core's own rules, section 7 of the contract). Every text a person or a reader writes must hold a non-space character: a blank field is refused, never carried.

answer_version.description: the version of this answer shape

run_id.description: the run this answer belongs to; record-answer refuses another run's id

session_id.description: the executor's session, copied from the adapter's answer_fields.session_id; record-answer refuses one that differs from the input's invocation.session_id

questions.description: the questions the executor put to the owner in this run, each with the scope doc's ledger line ids it touches (the shared E14-11 check refuses one that re-asks a decided line)

answer.description: the owner's answer, or null when he gave none

lines.description: lines the executor asserts, each with its trace (the shared E14-11 check); inspect-v2 writes no line from them, so a run usually carries none

row.description: the readers row the owner named for this run; record-answer refuses one that differs from the input's station.row

owner_word.description: present only for an outside row: the owner's word as the input carried it, byte for byte (record-answer refuses any other, and refuses it on a Claude row). It authorizes nothing here: the request's `authorized` flag came from the input alone.

lanes.description: the lenses of the calls this run's `request` built, every one of them: `traceability`, `code-book`, `repo-reality` (the Claude lane's three) or `paper` (an outside row's one call for the two paper lenses) and `repo-reality`; record-answer refuses a list that is not the built requests' lenses (lanes-mismatch), and a fleet with no result for a built call ends the run lane-down

adjudications.description: the executor's verify pass, one entry per finding it adjudicated. A finding is named `<call id>#<n>`, n its 1-based position in that result's findings. `confirmed` and `plausible` keep it with that label (the only source of either label); `refuted` drops it and counts it; `question` turns it into a QUESTION note. Every outside finding and every Claude-lane BLOCKER and MAJOR whose citation holds needs an entry (record-answer refuses a missing one, missing-adjudication), unless the no-record rule makes it a QUESTION note by itself. An entry cannot keep a finding whose citation matches nothing in the packet.

hunted_and_held.description: what the inspectors attacked that held up (v1's anti-rubber-stamp line, rule 10: mandatory in every run), in the executor's words from the replies; printed in the chat block and the verdict mirror

bottom_line.description: two or three sentences for the chat block and the verdict mirror: the plan's state and what to do next; mandatory in every run

results.description: the readers' results, one per lens call, copied from each call's READERS: line and reply

call_id.description: the reader call id the request carried; null is accepted by the schema so that record-answer can refuse it by name (independence: a finding with no reader call id has no reader)

effective_model.description: the READERS: line's effective model id; null ends the run `no-effective-model`, with no stamp

status.description: the READERS: line's status; absent reads as a reply that arrived. Anything but `ok` ends the run `lane-down` and nothing is triaged

reason.description: the result's reason, carried into a `lane-down` stop

raw_path.description: the raw copy readers filed for an outside call

location.description: `<packet file>:<line>` in the numbered packet (`build-doc.md:12`), or a workspace-relative `file:line` for a repo-reality finding; null for a concern without location, which never reaches the result

lens.description: on an outside row's paper call: which of the two paper lenses the finding came from, when the reply says

quote.description: the cited text, when the reply quotes it: a citation whose line does not carry it is refuted; one whose line carries it shows only that the text exists, and its label is still the executor's adjudication
